raw_response: {"sentences":[{"text":"Leaving the Conciergerie behind, head for Sainte-Chapelle, about a four-minute walk away.","source_id":"GLUE_NAV","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":4},{"text":"In August 1239, two Dominican friars reached Paris with a crate carried all the way from Venice, and for the final stretch King Louis took it onto his own shoulders — barefoot, dressed as a penitent.","source_id":"a185186e-905e-4066-b8d3-b0cfe52c14fe","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"You can still see that very scene inside, in the Relics of the Passion window on the chapel's south side.","source_id":"a185186e-905e-4066-b8d3-b0cfe52c14fe","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"Then he threw a week-long reception to celebrate.","source_id":"a185186e-905e-4066-b8d3-b0cfe52c14fe","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"Inside that crate, so the story went, were Christ's crown of thorns, fragments of the True Cross, and a nail from the crucifixion.","source_id":"6c03a747-d6bc-41fd-a7be-4f77b847481c","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"Louis had bought them from the bankrupt Byzantine Empire, and the price tells you exactly what mattered to him — 135,000 livres for the relics, another 100,000 for the silver Grand-Chasse to hold them, and just 40,000 to build and glaze the whole chapel around them.","source_id":"a185186e-905e-4066-b8d3-b0cfe52c14fe","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4,"also_cites":["6c03a747-d6bc-41fd-a7be-4f77b847481c"]},{"text":"He raised it between 1242 and 1248, and it's the only part of the island's medieval palace to survive whole — its slender spire shoots up above the Palais so steeply it looks like the choir of a cathedral that's been lopped off.","source_id":"6c03a747-d6bc-41fd-a7be-4f77b847481c","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"Step inside and there are really two chapels stacked together — a plain lower one built for the servants, and up a spiral staircase, the upper chapel reserved for the king and his court.","source_id":"6ae3bf26-cf36-414f-a10f-809bba4acc3c","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"Up there the walls are almost nothing but stained glass, and the stone that carries all that weight was deliberately split into clusters of pencil-thin columns so it looks impossibly fragile.","source_id":"6ae3bf26-cf36-414f-a10f-809bba4acc3c","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"There are 1,113 panels in all, two-thirds of them original, the rest from a nineteenth-century restoration.","source_id":"0c35674e-7d27-49ad-bdc6-1bbff4c3eec0","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"Together they run through nearly the whole Bible — Genesis on the north wall, the Passion of Christ at the east end, the relics' own history on the south, and the Apocalypse blazing in the rose window.","source_id":"0c35674e-7d27-49ad-bdc6-1bbff4c3eec0","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"The names of the glaziers who filled these walls are all lost.","source_id":"f9ed43cd-ef11-4623-b9aa-cc855cecf438","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"But the art historian Louis Grodecki teased three separate workshops out of the styles.","source_id":"f9ed43cd-ef11-4623-b9aa-cc855cecf438","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"The first gave the apse and most of the north wall its supple forms and simplified faces.","source_id":"f9ed43cd-ef11-4623-b9aa-cc855cecf438","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"The second, the Master of the Ezekiel Window, worked the Ezekiel, Daniel and Kings windows in elongated figures and angular drapery.","source_id":"f9ed43cd-ef11-4623-b9aa-cc855cecf438","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"The third, the Master of Judith and Esther, added the Job window too, with subtler faces and the feel of an illuminated manuscript.","source_id":"f9ed43cd-ef11-4623-b9aa-cc855cecf438","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"When the sun pours through, the blues and reds scatter across the interior until you feel wrapped in a swarm of brilliant butterflies.","source_id":"6ae3bf26-cf36-414f-a10f-809bba4acc3c","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"It's a favourite spot now for classical concerts, and a ticket booked a day or so ahead spares you the long queue.","source_id":"0c35674e-7d27-49ad-bdc6-1bbff4c3eec0","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"It hasn't always been treated so tenderly.","source_id":"6c03a747-d6bc-41fd-a7be-4f77b847481c","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"During the Revolution it was stripped of its holiness and put to work as a flour warehouse, then sensitively restored in the mid-nineteenth century as one of the great achievements of French High Gothic.","source_id":"6c03a747-d6bc-41fd-a7be-4f77b847481c","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"In the Second World War the glass came down and was hidden away for safekeeping.","source_id":"1ad1af2f-d9c3-4ede-aa28-76e6b1221f03","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"When it went back up in 1945, workers coated it in varnish to guard against bombing dust and scratches.","source_id":"1ad1af2f-d9c3-4ede-aa28-76e6b1221f03","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"Over the decades that varnish darkened, dimming images that were already fading.","source_id":"1ad1af2f-d9c3-4ede-aa28-76e6b1221f03","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"So in 2008 a seven-year, ten-million-euro programme set out to undo the damage.","source_id":"330c1038-505f-4ecf-a52b-2be84754b895","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"Half the money came from private donors, half from the Villum Foundation.","source_id":"330c1038-505f-4ecf-a52b-2be84754b895","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"Crews cleaned and preserved every panel, scrubbed the façade stone, conserved the sculpture, and slipped an innovative layer of thermoformed glass outside the medieval windows to shield them.","source_id":"330c1038-505f-4ecf-a52b-2be84754b895","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"The flamboyant west rose window was finished in 2015, timed for the 800th anniversary of Saint Louis's birth.","source_id":"330c1038-505f-4ecf-a52b-2be84754b895","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"As for the relics that started all this, they've moved on — kept now in the treasury of Notre-Dame, brought out only a few days a year, including Good Friday.","source_id":"6c03a747-d6bc-41fd-a7be-4f77b847481c","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4}]}
